description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. `execute()` has no active profile set — it runs every profile's primitives and the reader recognises all six block heads regardless of profile — so the declaration-slot guard cannot be gated on one, and `spec/grammar.md:408` (maintainer ruling #833) says it must not be: "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner". So `define ask` halts at phase-1 registration with `ol-reserved-word` and the `ask` call on line 4 never runs. This fixture was added because a mutation removing profile keywords from the runtime's built-in-name lookup passed the ENTIRE conformance corpus: `sprites/reserved-procedures-with-sprites` and its `-without-sprites` pair are both `"check": true`, so nothing in the corpus executed one of these names. That is still the only reason this fixture exists, and it still holds. THE RESIDUAL THIS FIXTURE DOCUMENTED IS CLOSED (issue #841). It used to record that `check()` and `execute()` disagreed for 32 of the registry's names under `profiles: ["core-language"]` alone — `check()` accepting what `execute()` rejected — because `checker-reserved-word.ts` composed its own profile-gated answer to "what is a built-in name" while the runtime swept every profile. #841 deleted that second composition: both stages now call one exported predicate, `@openlogo/parser`'s `isBuiltInName`. Re-measured by sweeping EVERY name in `spec/built-in-names.json` through `define <name>` at both stages under `["core-language"]`, with the sweep sanity-asserted in both directions (`myproc` accepted by both, `print` rejected by both): every name rejected by both stages, none accepted by check alone, none by execute alone. The count is deliberately not restated here -- it is the manifest's length, which the CI gate already holds. The count history is kept deliberately, because it is the point. An earlier revision said 22 rather than 32; that figure came from a hand-picked probe list rather than a registry sweep and undercounted by ten. Sampling instead of sweeping is the same defect this fixture exists to document, so the correction stayed recorded rather than being quietly applied — and the figure above is a sweep for the same reason.

diagnostics.message: ask is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
